column1: # Every difference between the two derivative tables, and why it is a difference and not a gap.
# Read by `scripts/vjp-parity.mjs`, one row per key: the marker (the operator's name, or the token
# a written operation is spelled with), the owner, and the reason. A key that is a difference and is
# not here is the debt that check exists to catch -- a law with no engine rule behind it, or an
# engine rule with no law. The three fields are the shape `known_fail` uses in the test plans (the
# mark, who owns it, why), and a wildcard is refused: a reader must be able to ask "why is this one
# allowed" about every row without asking anyone.
# The rows are one of these, and the reason says which:
#   甲  a gap this account is not allowed to leave open. None is left: `pick_at` was the one that
#       was, and the merge that closed it (`lane-pickatvjp`) took this file's row with it -- which
#       is the rule for the whole file, see below.
#   乙  the law belongs to the library alone: the operator is machinery the engine's own rules
#       build (`:tangent/*`, `:struct/*`, `cast_like`, ...), or it answers an integer or a mask and
#       has no tangent to carry.
#   丙  the rule belongs to the engine alone: the library's forward half (`rulesets.jvp`) files no
#       `jvp_<op>`, so the reverse question is never asked of the library at all.
# A row leaves this file the moment it stops holding a difference -- the law landed, the engine row
# landed, or the key derivation moved the row under another marker. A row that stays past that
# point is not harmless: it carries an owner and a reason, so it reads exactly like a live row, and
# the list stops being an account of what is still owed. That is why `scripts/vjp-parity.mjs`
# prints `stale=<n>` on every reading and `--strict` fails on a non-zero count.
# marker
column3: reason

column1: # ---- 乙: the tangent space's own operators (design principles 9.9) -----------------------------
# A gradient is summed and written with these, so a rule for them is a rule about the *tangent*
# space, and only the engine's rules build tangent nodes. A program cannot write one: they are
# declared with no export (`:tangent/*` in the core, `internal(...)` in the tensor module).
tangent/add_arr
column3: the tangent space's own sum: only a rule builds one, no program writes one

column1: tangent/zeros_arr
column3: the tangent space's own zero: only a rule builds one, no program writes one

column1: tangent/scatter_add_arr
column3: the tangent space's own scatter: only a rule builds one, no program writes one

column1: tangent/scatter_slice_arr
column3: the tangent space's own slice scatter: only a rule builds one

column1: tangent/scatter_take_arr
column3: the tangent space's own row scatter: only a rule builds one

column1: struct/append_arr
column3: the loop-state rewrite's append: a graph-machinery node, not a program's word

column1: struct/append_arr_owned
column3: the in-place form of that append: the same rewritten loop, same machinery

column1: struct/append_arr_in_place
column3: the in-place rebinding's append: the same rewritten loop, same machinery

column1: struct/copy_arr
column3: the private copy a rewritten loop starts from: machinery, the identity on values

column1: struct/concat_arr
column3: the array concatenation the graph builder writes: machinery, not a program's word

column1: # ---- 乙: the tensor module's internal rules (declared with no export) --------------------------
sum_to
column3: a reduction to an operand's shape, written by the engine's own rules

column1: broadcast_like
column3: a spread to an operand's shape, written by the engine's own rules

column1: expand_axis
column3: a spread along an axis, written by the engine's own reduction rules

column1: cast_like
column3: an element-type change between two rules' nodes, written by the engine

column1: permute_inverse
column3: the inverse permutation a permute's adjoint needs, written by the engine

column1: # ---- 乙: the operators the front end introduces (no source construct of that name) --------------
# The three the shape flip put in front of a differentiated value: a member read (`.x`, `.0`) and a
# conversion (`as`) are written as source constructs of *other* names, and the front end hands each
# of them to the engine as an operator of its own (`:op/access`, `:op/access_key`, `:op/cast`). The
# library's forward half files a `jvp_<op>` law per operator a program writes; no program writes one
# of these, so there is nothing for it to file and its table legitimately answers none of the three.
# The reverse question is still asked, because a differentiated value passes *through* such a node
# (design principles 9.9): `memberReadVjp` and `castVjp` (src/stdlib/std/builtin/operators/
# derivative.cpp) are the engine's own rules for them, and the engine's leg is the only leg there is.
access
column3: the member read by place the front end introduces (`:op/access`); no source operator of that name exists, so the law half files nothing and the engine's `memberReadVjp` is the rule

column1: access_key
column3: the same read by name (`:op/access_key`): the field is the front end's operand, not a source construct, so no `jvp_` law can be filed; the engine's `memberReadVjp` is the rule

column1: cast
column3: the conversion the front end introduces (`:op/cast`); the destination is a fact of the node, and no source operator names it, so the engine's `castVjp` is the reverse rule

column1: # ---- 乙: locally constant, or a value with no tangent space -----------------------------------
# `design principles 9.9`: a reading of a shape, a comparison and a label are locally constant in
# the value they read, so their contribution to a gradient is exactly zero. The engine files a rule
# that answers no gradient because the pullback visits any operator one of whose inputs is active --
# without the row it would refuse a shape query in a loss whose contribution is zero. A transposition
# law has nothing to put on that side: the library's forward half states the same fact by not
# filing a `jvp_*`.
# `dim` left it on 2026-11-22, when the comparison read `stdlib/rulesets/vmap.cml` for the first
# time: `#vmap_rule_dim` files `dim<axis>(x)` under `dim@1`, so the key is one both tables answer
# and the row had stopped holding a difference. The engine keeps its rule, and 9.9 is still why it
# answers zero; what changed is that the file states that fact and the comparison now reads it.
zeros_like
column3: locally constant in its operand: the zero array is the same for every value

column1: ones_like
column3: locally constant in its operand: the ones array is the same for every value

column1: numel
column3: answers an integer: a discrete value's derivative is zero by definition

column1: shape
column3: answers an integer list: a discrete value's derivative is zero by definition

column1: one_hot
column3: its input is a label: locally constant, the rows do not move with it

column1: strict_eq
column3: a comparison: a boolean has no tangent space to carry

column1: strict_neq
column3: a comparison: a boolean has no tangent space to carry

column1: ge
column3: a comparison: a boolean has no tangent space to carry

column1: gt
column3: a comparison: a boolean has no tangent space to carry

column1: le
column3: a comparison: a boolean has no tangent space to carry

column1: lt
column3: a comparison: a boolean has no tangent space to carry
the conversion's destination is `i32`, a discrete type with no tangent space

column1: int
column3: the conversion's destination is `int`, a discrete type with no tangent space

column1: # ---- 丙: the engine answers and the library's forward half cannot reach it ----------------------
# `rulesets.jvp` files no `jvp_<op>` for any of these, and the forward walk refuses a step it has no
# rule for, so a program that meets one of them is stopped by the library *before* the reverse
# question is asked. The law is therefore the engine's alone, and the engine's leg is the only leg
# there is. The row is listed one operator at a time rather than as a class because the day one of
# them gains a `jvp_*`, the reverse side becomes a gap and this file must say so by not holding it.
# That is how this block shrinks: twenty-two rows left it on 2026-11-14, when the laws they were
# waiting for landed and the keys they named became keys both tables answer (`abs`, `divide`,
# `erf`, `erfc`, `gelu`, `linear`, `log`, `max`, `max_axis`, `maximum`, `mean`, `min`, `min_axis`,
# `minimum`, `neg`, `rsqrt`, `sqrt`, `sum_axis`, `transpose`, `where`, and the two axis markers
# `argmax_axis`/`argmin_axis`, whose key now lands under `argmax`/`argmin`). The ones left are the
# ones still owed. `layer_norm` left it on 2026-11-20, when `rulesets/jvp.cml#jvp_layer_norm` landed
# beside the reverse rule the engine already had, so `layer_norm` is now a key both tables answer.
# `argmax`, `argmin`, `concat` and `unsqueeze` left it on 2026-11-22, when the comparison stopped
# reading two rulesets by name and read `stdlib/rulesets/` instead: `#vmap_rule_argmax`,
# `#vmap_rule_argmin`, `#vmap_rule_concat` and `#vmap_rule_unsqueeze` file `argmax@1`, `argmin@1`,
# `concat@2` and `unsqueeze@1`. Those rows were not recording a decision about the forward half;
# they were recording a file no line of the comparison opened.
pow
column3: the law is filed under `^` for `:op/pow_d`; `tensor:pow` has no `jvp_` of its own

column1: slice_sub
column3: no `jvp_slice_sub`: the library's forward half stops a program before the reverse is asked

column1: idx_take
column3: the subscript read's forward law is `jvp_idx_arr` for the two-word form; the slab form has no `jvp_*`

column1: # ---- 丙: the model operators (`modules/nn`), none of which the rulesets file for ---------------
batch_norm_train
column3: `nn`: a forward law needs the per-channel affine `gamma*xhat+beta` over `[N,C,H,W]`, i.e. a `[C]` vector applied to axis 1, and every stated broadcast right-aligns (`tensor/kernels/elementwise.cpp`, `BroadcastPlan`) so a `[C]` operand meets `W`; the only operators that index the channel axis are `batch_norm_train` and its gradient, and the gradient's transpose needs second-order terms of the same operator -- recorded in `src/stdlib/rulesets/jvp.cml`

column1: softmax_cross_entropy
column3: `nn`: the engine's `softmax_cross_entropy_grad` allocates **Float32** for its result whatever the logits' element type is (`nn/losses.cpp`, the `TypeCode::Float32` at both allocation sites), so a law's answer is `f32` while the cotangent port it must fill is the element type the walk hands; measured on the host, the backward graph refuses with "The value the graph 'split_of_jvp_of___g_369___backward' hands on has type 'f32', and the graph declares 'float'". A law cannot name the type it is right in until that kernel follows its operand's dtype, which is a change in the engine this lane may not make.

column1: softmax_cross_entropy_labels
column3: `nn`: the same kernel and the same wall as the row above (`softmax_cross_entropy_labels` shares `softmax_cross_entropy_grad`), measured with the same sentence; the label form differs only in that its target is an integer array, which is not the operand whose type matters here.

column1: # ---- 甲, settled elsewhere: the rows another lane owns ----------------------------------------
log_d
column3: the law is filed for the backward half only (`rulesets/transpose.cml#log_d_t`); the engine's derivative table has no `log_d` row, and no reading asks it for one

column1: pow_d
column3: the law is filed for the backward half only (`rulesets/transpose.cml#pow_d_t`); `tensor:pow`'s forward question is answered at `^`, and the engine has no `pow_d` row

column1: max_axis_stated
column3: `rulesets/transpose.cml#max_axis_stated_t` files the reverse law and the engine's table has no row for the stated key: the stated readings in `test/plans/feat/compile/stated_extents.plan.toml` ask the library

column1: min_axis_stated
column3: `rulesets/transpose.cml#min_axis_stated_t` files it; `min_axis_stated` is `max_axis_stated`'s rule with the mask flipped, so the engine row and this one are one decision

column1: mean_stated
column3: `rulesets/transpose.cml#mean_stated_t` files it; the engine has no row for the stated key, and the whole-tensor mean is answered through `mean_axis`

column1: sum_axis_stated
column3: `rulesets/transpose.cml#sum_axis_stated_t` files it; the engine has no row for the stated key, while `sum_stated`'s forward rule answers the whole-tensor form
